reason: This passage from Ruth describes a famine during the judges' period and follows the personal narratives of Naomi, Ruth, and Boaz. While there is suffering (the famine), the text contains no depiction of leaders addressing the Hebrew people and telling them their suffering is their fault. When Naomi expresses grief about her circumstances, she attributes her misfortune to God's actions ('the hand of the Lord has gone forth against me'), not to any fault of the people. The narrative focuses on individual redemption and God's providence rather than on leaders assigning blame to the people for their hardship.
